at_running_time_ms.description: Programme running time to open the break on. Omit to roll now.

return_to.description: Source to rejoin afterwards. Omit to return to whatever is on air.

uri.description: File path or URI of the clip to roll.

AdStatus.description: An ad break, either armed for a future cue or currently on air.

on_air.description: False while it is prerolled and waiting for its cue.

return_to.description: Source to return to when the ad ends. None returns to the slate.

id.description: The name this filter answers to afterwards. A slug, and yours to pick.

params.description:
The filter's own settings. What goes in here is the filter's business,
not the core's.

programme.description: Filter the programme rather than one source.

side.description:
`input` puts it before the proxy boundary, where the thumbnail sees it
too; `programme` puts it on this source's programme branch only.

source.description:
The source to hang it on. Leave it out and set `programme` to filter
everything that goes out.

type.description: A filter type id, as `plugin.list` and `core.api` `kinds` report them.

AddOutputRequest.description:
`output.add`. The id and the URL are the whole of it for an RTMP
destination; anything else a kind understands rides in `params`.

policy.description:
Reconnect policy: "own" retries quickly, for servers you run; "cdn"
backs off harder, for platforms that penalise hammering.

uri.description: rtmp:// or rtmps:// URL including the stream key.

source.description:
A local directory with `gmx-plugin.toml` at its root. Git, an index and
a signed release are Phase 5; this takes a path.

id.description:
Stable id used by `program.take` and `source.remove`. Lowercase
letters, digits and dashes. Derived from the name or the host when
omitted, with a numeric suffix if that is taken.

kind.description:
"web" renders the URL as a page in the browser sidecar, the same as
writing `web+` in front of it. "auto" or omitted works the protocol out
from the URL.

name.description: Name shown to an operator. Defaults to the host of the URL.

superimpose.description:
Websites only: "auto" lets the mixer decode the page's own video
outside the browser and draw the page over the top, which saves about a
CPU core. "off" is the default.

uri.description: Stream URL, file path, or with kind "web" the address of a page.

AudioSetParams.description:
`source.audio.set` takes an id as well as the levels: the id comes off the
path on REST and out of the params on `/rpc`, and both land in one object.

gain.description:
The operator's fader for the whole source, 0.0 to 10.0. Omit to leave
it where it is.

media.description:
Gain per video underneath, by position. A null entry, or a list shorter
than the number of videos, leaves those alone: `[null, 0.0]` silences
the second video and touches nothing else.

muted.description:
Mute the whole source. Held apart from the fader, so unmuting comes
back to the level that was set.

page.description: Gain on a superimposed page's own sound.

CanvasInfo.description: The canvas every source is scaled onto and every output leaves by.

source.description: None means this cell is the program return.

ConversionState.description: One conversion, in flight or remembered after it finished.

error.description:
Set only on `failed`, shown to the operator verbatim: "no AAC encoder
available" is worth more than "conversion failed".

progress.description: 0.0 to 1.0, position over duration, both read off the pipeline.

CoreInfo.description: `core.info`: what this core is, what it can do, and where its edges are.

features.description:
Feature strings a client can branch on: multiview, snapshot, uploads,
mcp, browser, exec-sources, rehearsal, tokens.

rehearsal.description:
True when the core was started with `--rehearsal`, which refuses
`output.add` and accepts rehearsal tokens.

token.description: Present when the request carried a token the core recognises.

version.description: The build's own version, as in Cargo.toml.

Ext.description:
The `ext` table from 03 section 6.

Every key is off by default. A terminal UI takes meters and tally and
declines multiview; a Stream Deck takes tally only; an agent takes nothing.

multiview.description:
The mosaic: binary frames and `event/multiview.layout`. `false` or
omitted builds nothing.

FilterIdRequest.description: `filter.remove`, and anything else that names one filter.

FilterRecord.description: One filter as the core reports it.

Flush.description: `event/flush`: the end of a batch. A client renders here and not before.

seq.description: The sequence number of the last event in the batch.

GoLiveRequest.description: `program.golive`: add the page, add the destination, take the page.

id.description: Source id. Derived from the host when omitted.

rtmp.description:
Where to send the programme. Added as an output unless one already
sends there. Omit to leave the outputs alone.

url.description: The page to put on air. Plain http(s); `web+` is added here.

output.description: The output that was created or reused, if one was asked for.

source.description: The source that was created or reused.

state.description: Where the source is now. It goes to programme as soon as it is live.

limit.description: How many takes to return, newest first. At most 100.

InstanceRecord.description: One running instance and its cost.

plugin.description:
The plugin it belongs to. Carried on the instance as well as on the
plugin, because `plugin.stats` is a flat list and a caller holding one
row should not have to go back for the name.

Limits.description:
The ceilings a client should plan against rather than discover by being
refused.

event_queue.description: How many events the bus holds before a slow client is told to resync.

max_call_secs.description:
Longest any method blocks before it answers. The tightest client
default in the wild, so nothing here can time out a client that used
its own.

max_gain.description:
Loudest a fader can be asked for. Out of range is clamped to this
rather than refused.

max_upload_bytes.description: Largest upload the media endpoint accepts, in bytes.

duration_secs.description:
How long before it goes back down. A minute by default, which is long
enough to reproduce a fault and short enough that a forgotten firehose
stops on its own.

categories.description:
The categories actually raised, which is what the caller asked for
with anything GStreamer does not know dropped.

LogSetRequest.description: `log.set`. Name an instance or a target, not both.

instance.description:
A plugin instance: a source or an output id. Its lines carry the id,
so raising this one raises only that camera.

level.description:
`off`, `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug`, `trace`, or `default` to stop
overriding this one.

target.description:
A module path prefix such as `godwinmix::mixer`. The longest match
wins, so a more specific override still beats a broader one.

conversion.description:
Where a conversion of this file stands, None when none was asked for in
this process's lifetime.

duration_ms.description:
None when the file could not be inspected; it is still listed, because
an operator would rather see a clip they cannot read the length of than
wonder why it is missing.

faststart.description:
The converted copy's absolute path when one exists on disk. This is
what "add as source" should prefer over `path`.
Whether the moov atom comes first (a player can start before the whole
file arrives). None for a non-ISO container, never a reason to convert
on its own. See `convert::moov_first`.

name.description: Name shown in the UI, relative to the library root.

path.description: Absolute path, which is what gets handed back to the ad break API.

reasons.description: Why it is not, in words an operator can act on. Empty when it is.

video_codec.description:
Short codec name of the first video stream ("h264", "vp9"), None when
there is no video or it could not be inspected.

web_safe.description:
True when the file needs no conversion to play in a browser: H.264 plus
AAC (or no audio) in an MP4. See `convert::web_safety`.

error.description:
Set when the directory itself could not be read, so the UI can say why
the list is empty instead of just showing nothing.

Meters.description:
`event/meters`: the programme bus and every source, in one message at 10
per second, rather than one message per meter as the legacy stream sends.

program.description: Peak dBFS per channel on the programme bus.

sources.description: Peak dBFS per channel, per source id.

ad.description: Present while an ad break is armed or running.

program.description: Source currently on program, or None while the slate is showing.

running_time_ms.description:
Program pipeline running time. Cues are scheduled against this, not
against wall clock, so a client can place a break on a known frame.

fps.description: Frames per second, 1 to 30. The core clamps to what the mosaic runs at.

MultiviewExt.description: `ext.multiview`. Accepts `false` to mean off, or an object.

MultiviewLayout.description: `event/multiview.layout`: how to read the binary frames that follow.

id.description:
Stable for as long as the cells are unchanged, and carried in the
header of every frame, so a client that falls behind can tell which
layout a late frame belongs to.

cells.description:
Cell index to source id, in reading order. Cell 0 is the program return
when it is enabled.

fps.description: Frame rate of the mosaic, so the UI can size its own expectations.

NameRequest.description: `media.convert` and `media.remove` name a file rather than an id.

name.description:
File name as it appears in the media listing. The REST layer puts it
in the path, where the transform rule calls it `id`, so both spellings
are read.

queue_secs.description:
Seconds of encoded data waiting in the pre-muxer queue. A number that
climbs and stays high means the destination cannot keep up.

PipelineDot.description:
What `pipeline.dot` answers with on `/rpc`. The REST route serves the same
graph as `text/vnd.graphviz`, so `gmx dot | dot -Tsvg` needs no unwrapping.

dot.description: The graph itself, in the dot language.

PipelineRequest.description:
Which pipeline to look at. A source id, an output id, `programme` or
`multiview`. `pipeline.list` says what is running.

PluginDescription.description: The whole of one plugin, for an agent about to use it.

instances.description: Every running instance of it, with what it costs.

manifest.description: The manifest as JSON, every table of it.

problem.description: Why it is not loaded, when it is not.

provides.description:
The type ids it contributes: what goes in `type` on a source, an output
or a filter.

schemas.description: Per provide id, its settings schema.

skills.description: Per provide id, the description line from its SKILL.md.

tools.description:
Its MCP tools, as `gmx_<plugin>_<tool>`. Reachable with `search_tools`;
never in the hot list.

plugins_dir.description: Where plugins are read from on this machine.

PluginName.description:
Anything that names one plugin.

The field is `id` because that is what the REST layer fills in from
`/api/v1/plugins/{id}`, and a plugin's id is its name: the namespace of
every id it contributes. `name` is accepted as well, for a JSON-RPC caller
who wrote the obvious thing.

PluginRecord.description: One plugin as the core reports it.

instances.description: Every running instance of it, with what it costs.

problem.description: Why it is not loaded, when it is not.

provides.description:
The type ids it contributes: what goes in `type` on a source, an output
or a filter.

tools.description:
Its MCP tools, as `gmx_<plugin>_<tool>`. Reachable with `search_tools`;
never in the hot list.

provides.description: What went with it, so a caller can see the blast radius.

schemas.description: The JSON Schema every surface renders, one per provide.

ProgramState.description:
What `program.get` answers with, and what `program.take` returns so that no
follow up read is needed.

ad.description: Present while an ad break is armed or on air.

previous.description: The previous source, which is what `program.revert` would take back to.

program.description: Source on air, or null for the slate.

running_time_ms.description: Programme pipeline running time, in milliseconds.

Resync.description: `event/resync`: the client fell behind and the stream has a hole in it.

from_seq.description:
The last sequence number the client is known to have. Everything after
it was dropped; re-subscribe for a fresh snapshot.

position_ms.description:
Milliseconds from the start of the clip. Off either end is clamped
rather than refused, so a scrubber flicked past the end lands there.

secs.description: How far back to read, in seconds. An hour by default, a day at most.

params.description: The settings to apply. Only the keys named are changed.

settings.description: Only the keys named are changed.

oneOf.description:
Loud enough to page someone. Nothing raises it yet; it is here so the
severity ladder in `protocol.json` is the one 03 section 6 names.

Snapshot.description: `event/snapshot`: the full state, and where in the stream it sits.

SnapshotRequest.description: `snapshot.get` on `/rpc` and through MCP. The REST route serves the same bytes raw, because an `` tag cannot read base64 out of JSON.

allow_large.description: Permit a width above the `[snapshot] max_width` ceiling.

force.description: Ignore the per client rate limit for this one request.

id.description: "sheet", "program", or a source id. A `.jpg` on the end is accepted.

width.description:
Scale down to this many pixels across, keeping the aspect. Never
enlarges. Omit for the `[snapshot] default_width` of 320, which is
enough to see who is in shot; `width: 0` for the cell's own size.

SourceAudioState.description:
What a source's audio controls read back as, which is what the audio
endpoint answers with.

Wider than `SourceAudio` because the fader and the mute apply to every
source, while the page and media balance belongs only to a superimposed one.
Every number here is read off the elements after the request landed, so a
request whose gain was clamped answers with the gain that took effect.

page.description:
Absent on anything but a superimposed source, which is the only kind
with separate sounds to balance.

SourcePositionState.description:
Where a seekable source has got to, which is what the seek endpoint answers
with.

Both numbers are read back off the pipeline after the seek has landed, not
taken from the request. A seek snaps to a key unit, so the frame an operator
asked for and the frame they got are rarely the same millisecond, and a
scrubber drawn from the request would sit a little away from the picture.

duration_ms.description: Absent while the demuxer has not worked the duration out yet.

oneOf.description: Pipeline is up but no media has arrived yet.
Buffers arriving within the stall timeout.

Was live, then went quiet. Its program pad is held at alpha 0 so the
slate shows through rather than a frozen frame.
The input pipeline errored. A retry is scheduled.

audio_idle_ms.description:
Same for audio. `None` here while `has_audio` is true means the source
advertised an audio track that never produced a decoded sample.

cell.description: Index into the multiview grid, or None while the source has no cell.

gain.description:
The operator's fader for this source, 0.0 silent through 1.0 unity to a
ceiling of 10.0. Read back off the volume element rather than remembered,
so what the UI shows is what the pipeline is doing.

muted.description:
Muted by the operator. Held apart from the fader so that unmuting returns
the source to where it was rather than to unity.

position_ms.description:
Where this source has got to, and how long it runs, in milliseconds.
`None` on anything not seekable, and on a seekable source whose duration
the demuxer has not worked out yet.

seekable.description:
True when this source can be scrubbed. A file can be. A camera, an RTMP
feed or a page cannot, and asking one to is a mistake worth refusing
rather than quietly doing nothing.

video_idle_ms.description: Milliseconds since the last video buffer, or None if none has arrived.

SubscribeRequest.description: `core.subscribe`: which events, and which expensive streams.

events.description:
Event name patterns, matched against the part after `event/`. `*`
matches one or more characters: "program.*" matches `event/program.took`.
An empty list subscribes to everything.

ext.description:
The expensive streams this client wants. Nothing here runs unless a
client asks for it.

SubscribeResult.description: What `core.subscribe` answers with, before the snapshot arrives.

events.description: The event patterns now in force.

ignored_ext.description: `ext` keys this build ignored. Empty on a build that knows them all.

seq.description: The sequence number the snapshot that follows is current as of.

at_running_time_ms.description: Programme running time the cut landed on.

by.description: Token id that asked for it, or "core" when the mixer did it itself.

seq.description: Event sequence number the take was published under.

source.description: What went on air. Null is the slate.

at_running_time_ms.description:
Programme running time to land the cut on, in milliseconds. Omit for
immediate. Read the current running time from `core.info` or a status
snapshot first.

scene.description:
The scene to take, once scenes exist (11). Today a scene name is read
as a one item scene, which is to say as a source id, and `source` wins
when both are given.

source.description: Id of the source to put on air. Null or omitted cuts to the slate.

TokenInfo.description:
What the calling token is allowed to do, echoed back so a surface can grey
out what it cannot reach instead of discovering it at the first refusal.

confirm.description: "none" or "required": whether destructive calls need a confirm token.

profile.description: MCP tool profile this token is meant for: "standard" or "minimal".

description: The GodwinMix control protocol. One set of methods, events and types, whether the peer is a UI on /rpc, curl on /api/v1, the CLI, the MCP server or a plugin on stdio.

envelope.description: Keys accepted on every method, handled before a method runs.

confirm.description: The confirm_token from a -32020 refusal, valid 30 seconds. Only a token whose policy is confirm = required needs it.

dry_run.description: On any destructive method. Answers the diff it would make and would_change, against the live state, and changes nothing.

idempotency_key.description: On any mutating method. The answer is kept for 24 hours; a replay returns it with replayed: true. The same key with different params is -32602 with data.idempotency = mismatch.

trace_id.description: Carried into the answer, the X-Trace-Id header and the log line. Taken from the W3C traceparent header over HTTP, or generated.

errors.meaning: the envelope was not a JSON-RPC request
the params were wrong for this method
the core failed while handling the call
not in a state that allows this
the plugin did not declare that placement
the plugin died during the call
a protocol line was over 4 MiB
the change needs the instance restarted
a confirm token is needed first

events.name: event/snapshot
events.summary: The full state, and the sequence number it is current as of. Sent on subscribe and after any change the deltas cannot describe.

events.name: event/program.took
events.summary: The programme changed. Carries the running time the cut landed on, so a client can see how close a scheduled take was to its mark.

events.name: event/source.state
events.summary: A source moved between connecting, live, stalled and failed.

events.name: event/source.position
events.summary: How far through a seekable source has got, a few times a second. Never sent for a camera, which has no position to report.

events.name: event/output.state
events.summary: A destination connected, dropped or is retrying.

events.name: event/adbreak.changed
events.summary: An ad break was armed, went on air, or ended.

events.name: event/media.changed
events.summary: A file in the library was uploaded, deleted, or its conversion moved on.

events.name: event/meters
events.summary: Peak dBFS for the programme bus and every source, in one message at 10 per second. Replaces the two separate meter events on /ws.

events.name: event/tally
events.summary: Which sources are on programme, on preview, or off. Derived by the core so a Stream Deck does not have to.

events.name: event/alert
events.summary: Something an operator should see. Also written to the log and to the alert webhook.

events.name: event/multiview.layout
events.summary: How to read the binary frames that follow: the cells, and the layout id carried in every frame header.

events.name: event/multiview.frame

payload.description: 16 byte header then JPEG. Not a JSON message.

events.summary: A mosaic frame, as a binary WebSocket frame rather than JSON: a 16 byte little endian header (seq u32, layout id u32, programme running time in milliseconds u64) then the JPEG.

events.name: event/resync
events.summary: This client fell behind and events were dropped. Re-subscribe for a fresh snapshot; nothing between from_seq and the new snapshot arrives.

events.name: event/flush
events.summary: The end of a batch. Render here and not before, so a client never paints half an update.

ext.turns_on: the mosaic pipeline, built on the first subscriber and stopped on the last, plus event/multiview.layout and the binary frames
per source thumbnails from a node

filter.description: A green, blue or custom colour key

output.description: FLV over RTMP or RTMPS, the ingest every CDN takes
MPEG-TS over SRT, in caller or listener mode

source.description: An RTMP or RTMPS publisher, decoded with the hardware the machine has
A continuous stream: HLS, DASH, RTSP, SRT, RTP or UDP
A finite clip on disk or over HTTP, scrubbable, ending with EOS
A command whose process writes a container to stdout
A web page rendered as a live source, by the sidecar or by wpesrc
A web page drawn over the video it was playing, decoded here rather than in the browser
A test pattern and a tone, for the conformance harness

methods.name: adbreak.end
methods.summary: Cut a running ad short, or disarm one that is scheduled.

methods.name: adbreak.start
methods.summary: Interrupt the programme with a clip, then rejoin live when it ends.

methods.name: agent.state
methods.summary: The compact document written for agents: the programme, each source's state and a motion score saying how much its picture is changing.

methods.name: codec.list
methods.summary: Every codec and element in the catalogue, which of them this machine actually has, and what it would pick.

methods.name: core.api
methods.summary: Every method, event and type as JSON Schema. The same document as protocol.json and `godwinmix --api-info`.

methods.name: core.doctor
methods.summary: The environment checks: GStreamer, the elements, the config, the disk and the ports. The same list `gmx doctor` prints.

methods.name: core.info
methods.summary: What this core is, what it can do, and where its edges are.

methods.name: core.session_log
methods.summary: The append only record of everything that happened, back as far as you ask.

methods.name: core.shutdown
methods.summary: Stop the mixer, and with it the programme. Nothing else takes the show off air, so this is deliberately its own call.

methods.name: core.startup_report
methods.summary: How long each stage of the start took, and what was over the 250 ms mark.

methods.name: core.status
methods.summary: The full state: programme, every source, every output, the multiview grid, the encoder backend and any ad break.

methods.name: core.subscribe
methods.summary: Subscribe to the event stream. WebSocket only: the core answers event/snapshot then deltas, ending every batch with event/flush.

methods.name: filter.add
methods.summary: Hang a filter on one source or on the programme, live.

methods.name: filter.list
methods.summary: Every filter in place, with what it is and where it sits.

methods.name: filter.remove
methods.summary: Take a filter out of the pipeline.

methods.name: filter.set
methods.summary: Change a filter's settings in place. A filter that cannot take the change while running says so rather than being restarted behind your back.

methods.name: log.gst
methods.summary: Raise GStreamer's own debug categories for a while, then let them fall back on their own.

methods.name: log.levels
methods.summary: Every log level override in force, and the GStreamer categories still raised.

methods.name: log.set
methods.summary: Change one instance's or one module's log level while the mixer runs.

methods.name: media.convert
methods.summary: Transcode a library file to a web safe copy, in the background.

methods.name: media.list
methods.summary: The clips in the library, with durations and whether each has audio.

methods.name: media.remove
methods.summary: Delete a library file and its converted copy. Refused while it is a live source.

methods.name: media.upload
methods.summary: Stream a file into the library. HTTP only: the body is the file.

methods.name: output.add
methods.summary: Send the programme to another destination. The encoder is shared, so adding one costs nothing on air.

methods.name: output.get
methods.summary: One destination.

methods.name: output.list
methods.summary: Every destination, with its state, reconnect count and how much is buffered.

methods.name: output.reconnect
methods.summary: Drop and re-establish one destination's connection now, without waiting for its reconnect policy.

methods.name: output.remove
methods.summary: Stop sending to a destination and forget it. Other outputs are unaffected.

methods.name: pipeline.clock
methods.summary: The clock every pipeline is running against, and how far each one has got.

methods.name: pipeline.dot
methods.summary: One pipeline as a graphviz graph: every element, every pad and the caps negotiated between them.

methods.name: pipeline.latency
methods.summary: How much delay one pipeline is carrying, and which stage put it there.

methods.name: pipeline.list
methods.summary: Every pipeline running right now, by the name the other pipeline methods accept.

methods.name: pipeline.queues
methods.summary: Every queue in one pipeline with how full it is, fullest first. A queue that stays full is where the trouble is.

methods.name: plugin.add
methods.summary: Install a plugin from a local directory, while live. The directory is the one with gmx-plugin.toml at its root.

methods.name: plugin.describe
methods.summary: One plugin in full: its manifest, the settings schema of every provide, and the description from each SKILL.md.

methods.name: plugin.disable
methods.summary: Turn a plugin off without uninstalling it. It registers nothing and runs no process until it is enabled again.

methods.name: plugin.enable
methods.summary: Turn a plugin back on. It registers what it declares and its instances start.

methods.name: plugin.list
methods.summary: Every plugin installed, with what it provides and what each running instance is costing in cpu, memory, latency, dropped buffers and restarts.

methods.name: plugin.reload
methods.summary: Read a plugin's directory again and swap its running instances one at a time, with the freeze frame covering each.

methods.name: plugin.remove
methods.summary: Uninstall a plugin and unwind everything it registered: its provides, its tools, its panels, its hooks and its discovery matchers.

methods.name: plugin.settings.get
methods.summary: A plugin's settings as they stand, with its schema beside them.

methods.name: plugin.settings.set
methods.summary: Change a plugin's settings. A plugin that cannot take a change while running says so rather than being restarted behind your back.

methods.name: plugin.stats
methods.summary: Per instance cpu, memory, media latency, dropped buffers and restarts, refreshed once a second.

methods.name: program.get
methods.summary: What is on air, the programme running time, and what revert would go back to.

methods.name: program.golive
methods.summary: One call to put a web page on air: add the page, add the destination, and take the page as soon as it renders.

methods.name: program.history
methods.summary: The last hundred takes, newest first, with the token that asked for each.

methods.name: program.revert
methods.summary: Take back to the shot before this one.

methods.name: program.take
methods.summary: Put a source on programme. The cut is instant and the outgoing stream is not disturbed.

methods.name: snapshot.get
methods.summary: One JPEG: the whole contact sheet, the programme, or one source cut out of the mosaic.

methods.name: source.add
methods.summary: Add a source while the mixer runs. Answers with the id it got and the whole source record.

methods.name: source.audio.set
methods.summary: Move a source's audio: the fader, the mute, and for a superimposed page the balance between its own sound and the videos under it.

methods.name: source.get
methods.summary: One source. Refused with the ids that exist when there is no such source.

methods.name: source.list
methods.summary: Every source, with its state, whether it has video and audio, and its fader.

methods.name: source.remove
methods.summary: Remove a source. If it is on programme the mixer cuts to the slate first.

methods.name: source.seek
methods.summary: Move a seekable source to a position. Answers with where it actually landed.

godwinmix mcp, a thin adapter over these same methods
